title: Dominica's Small‐Scale Fisheries: Biological Sampling Underpins the Need for Balanced Fishing on Inshore and Offshore, Reef and Pelagic Species
content:
ABSTRACT

Dominica's small-scale fisheries provide vital food and income for coastal communities but face increasing pressure from climate-driven shifts in fish distributions, reef degradation, and extreme events such as Hurricane Maria in 2017, which caused catastrophic damage. In response to these challenges, a biological sampling programme was initiated in 2018–2019 to measure fish species landed by Dominican fishers across the island. The dataset, comprising 3007 measurements sampled at 12 landing sites, provides a detailed picture of catches and size distributions. These showed that for the key pelagic species dolphinfish (Coryphaena hippurus), 99% of individuals measured exceeded length-at-maturity, indicating generally sustainable exploitation. In contrast, some reef-associated species showed high proportions of small fish in landings—for example, 71% below length-at-maturity in blackfin snapper (Lutjanus buccanella). These patterns underline the importance of balanced fishing on inshore and offshore, reef and pelagic species. Strengthening long-term data collection will support evidence-based management to enhance climate resilience and ensure the ongoing sustainability of Dominica's fisheries.
